Courses, instructors and teaching periods of the Statistics curriculum of the PhD in Economics, Statistics and Data Science. First-year students attend courses with a final exam; second-year students attend reading groups. A short description of the contents is given where a syllabus is available. The [official website of the PhD programme](https://www.dems.unimib.it/en/programmes/post-lauream/phd-economics-statistics-and-data-science) remains the reference; detailed timetables are in the Google calendars for the [first year](https://calendar.google.com/calendar/embed?src=c_4223552c63dcc9f610371e23a4043a88a1573bc139d5d350f9569beabc41e77b%40group.calendar.google.com&ctz=Europe/Rome) and the [second year](https://calendar.google.com/calendar/embed?src=c_c815906ccefc45fb890f3b3e789db5bfeb36bd13b2cedce148536c16c160099c%40group.calendar.google.com&ctz=Europe/Rome).

Instructors without an affiliation are from the University of Milano-Bicocca. Rows in grey are potential courses from the Big Data & Analytics for Business curriculum, not yet confirmed for the Statistics curriculum.

## First year (cycle XLII)

```{=html}
<div class="crs-term">
  <h3 class="sem-group">Term I <span>· lectures 26 Oct – 18 Dec 2026 · exams 7 – 14 Jan 2027</span></h3>
  <details class="crs-row">
    <summary><span class="crs-main"><span class="crs-title">Mathematical Analysis I</span><span class="crs-who">Francesco Battistoni <span class="affil">(Univ. Cattolica)</span></span></span><span class="crs-side"><span class="chip chip-academia">Course</span><span class="crs-when">27 Oct – 12 Nov · 16 h</span></span></summary>
    <div class="crs-body">
      <p>Sequences and series of functions: pointwise and uniform convergence, uniform Cauchy condition, preservation of continuity and of the integral. Metric spaces, induced topology, compactness, completeness and density; normed spaces and the space C[0,1]. Cardinality, σ-algebras and Borel σ-algebras, measurable functions with values in a metric space.</p>
      <p class="crs-links"><a href="https://drive.google.com/file/d/16M0RGNawIcn2Jj8yEcw-xZvqY8wKyyvv/view">Syllabus (PDF)</a></p>
    </div>
  </details>
  <details class="crs-row">
    <summary><span class="crs-main"><span class="crs-title">Mathematical Analysis II</span><span class="crs-who">Carlo Alberto De Bernardi <span class="affil">(Univ. Cattolica)</span></span></span><span class="crs-side"><span class="chip chip-academia">Course</span><span class="crs-when">17 Nov – 10 Dec · 16 h</span></span></summary>
    <div class="crs-body">
      <p>Measurable functions and approximation by simple functions. Positive measures, completion, Lebesgue measure via the outer measure, Carathéodory's extension theorem. Lebesgue integral: monotone convergence, Fatou's lemma, dominated convergence, comparison with the Riemann integral. Absolute continuity, Radon–Nikodym theorem and Lebesgue decomposition. Exercises.</p>
      <p class="crs-links"><a href="https://drive.google.com/file/d/16M0RGNawIcn2Jj8yEcw-xZvqY8wKyyvv/view">Syllabus (PDF, common to Mathematical Analysis I–III)</a></p>
    </div>
  </details>
  <details class="crs-row">
    <summary><span class="crs-main"><span class="crs-title">Mathematical Analysis III</span><span class="crs-who">Enrico Miglierina <span class="affil">(Univ. Cattolica)</span></span></span><span class="crs-side"><span class="chip chip-academia">Course</span><span class="crs-when">14 – 18 Dec · 8 h</span></span></summary>
    <div class="crs-body">
      <p>Product measure and integration on product spaces; Tonelli and Fubini theorems with counterexamples. L<sup>p</sup> spaces, Hölder and Minkowski inequalities, completeness of L<sup>p</sup> for 1 ≤ p ≤ ∞; the example of ℓ<sup>p</sup>.</p>
      <p class="crs-links"><a href="https://drive.google.com/file/d/16M0RGNawIcn2Jj8yEcw-xZvqY8wKyyvv/view">Syllabus (PDF, common to Mathematical Analysis I–III)</a></p>
    </div>
  </details>
</div>
```

## Second year (cycle XLI)

```{=html}
<div class="crs-term">
  <h3 class="sem-group">Term I <span>· 26 Oct – 18 Dec 2026</span></h3>
  <details class="crs-row">
    <summary><span class="crs-main"><span class="crs-title">Approximate Bayesian Computational Methods</span><span class="crs-who">Augusto Fasano <span class="affil">(Univ. Torino and Collegio Carlo Alberto)</span></span></span><span class="crs-side"><span class="chip chip-academia-light">Reading group</span><span class="crs-when">Term I</span></span></summary>
    <div class="crs-body">
      <p>Theoretical and computational aspects of the most widely used approximate methods for Bayesian inference when the posterior is intractable or MCMC is computationally impractical, with a focus on binary and categorical regression. Four modules:</p>
      <ul>
        <li>Laplace approximation, Variational Bayes and Expectation Propagation: general principles and theoretical guarantees.</li>
        <li>Variational Bayes for binary regression: logit and probit models.</li>
        <li>Expectation Propagation in practice: the clutter problem and probit regression.</li>
        <li>Extensions to categorical data, dynamic settings and beyond.</li>
      </ul>
      <p class="crs-links"><a href="https://drive.google.com/file/d/1cwhLdL_OMDEscSRRN6H1S2F_MeOxRtsS/view">Syllabus with references (PDF)</a></p>
    </div>
  </details>
  <div class="crs-row"><div class="crs-sum"><span class="crs-main"><span class="crs-title">Probabilistic Preference Learning</span><span class="crs-who">Valeria Vitelli <span class="affil">(Univ. Oslo)</span></span></span><span class="crs-side"><span class="chip chip-academia-light">Reading group</span><span class="crs-when">Term I</span></span></div></div>
</div>
```
